title: Crash during shutdown in uninitialize_gdscript_module due to ref-counted singleton
body:
### Tested versions

-Reproducible in v4.6.1.mrlink5.mono.custom_build [cb200ef6d]

(This is a light fork of v4.6.1)

### System information

Godot v4.6.1.mrlink5.mono (cb200ef6d) - Windows 11 (build 26200) - Multi-window, 2 monitors - Direct3D 12 (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4090 (NVIDIA; 32.0.15.9186) - 13th Gen Intel(R) Core(TM) i9-13900K (32 threads) - 127.7 GiB memory

### Issue description

I was hitting intermittent (~40% of the time) crashes when godot was shutting down during `--import`. The crash stack was:

```
[0] RefCounted::unreference (F:\1\s\core\object\ref_counted.cpp:85)
[1] Variant::ObjData::unref (F:\1\s\core\variant\variant.cpp:1136)
[2] CowData<Variant>::_unref (F:\1\s\core\templates\cowdata.h:249)
[3] GDScriptLanguage::`scalar deleting destructor'
[4] uninitialize_gdscript_module (F:\1\s\modules\gdscript\register_types.cpp:178)
[5] uninitialize_modules (F:\1\s\modules\register_module_types.gen.cpp:309)
[6] Main::cleanup (F:\1\s\main\main.cpp:5180)
[7] widechar_main (F:\1\s\platform\windows\godot_windows.cpp:105)
[8] _main (F:\1\s\platform\windows\godot_windows.cpp:128)
[9] main (F:\1\s\platform\windows\godot_windows.cpp:140)
```

This seemed to get triggered by changes I made to the order that we initialize/uninitialize components in our GDExtension. I added some extra logging into the GDScriptLanguage destructor to find out which specific object being destroyed was causing it, and it was a godot::RefCounted object that we register/unregister as a singleton during MODULE_INITIALIZATION_LEVEL_SCENE initialize/uninitialize stage of our GDExtension.

Now the following is an AI generated summary that is part of my investigation, so feel free to take it with a grain of salt, but I can say that changing our object from godot::RefCounted to godot::Object did work around the problem. And I also applied the fix that it recommended it also fixed the problem. So I think there is evidence this explanation of the issue has some merit:

> GDScriptLanguage::finish() clears script_list and function_list but does not clear global_array, globals, named_globals, or global_array_empty_indexes. These containers hold Variant entries populated during GDScriptLanguage::init(), including GDExtension-registered classes and singletons added via _extension_loaded()
>
> The actual destruction of these containers is deferred to the implicit ~GDScriptLanguage() destructor, which runs much later when uninitialize_gdscript_module() calls memdelete(script_language_gd).
> 
> The problem is the teardown order in Main::cleanup():
> 
> 1. ScriptServer::finish_languages() --> calls GDScriptLanguage::finish()
> 2. GDExtensionManager::deinitialize_extensions(SCENE) --> unloads extension classes
> 3. unregister_scene_types() --> tears down ClassDB entries
> 4. uninitialize_modules(SERVERS) --> memdelete(script_language_gd) --> ~GDScriptLanguage()
> By step 4, many objects referenced by global_array have already been destroyed or had their class metadata removed in steps 2–3. When the Vector<Variant> destructor runs, it calls Variant::ObjData::unref() --> RefCounted::unreference() on freed or partially-torn-down objects, causing a use-after-free crash.

The following is the fix that I applied that stopped the crashing. But I do not have enough familiarity to say how correct it is, if at all:
```cpp
void GDScriptLanguage::finish() {
    // ... existing cleanup of script_list, function_list ...

    // Clear global arrays now while referenced objects (GDScriptNativeClass,
    // singletons) are still alive. If left for implicit destruction in
    // ~GDScriptLanguage(), the underlying objects may have already been freed
    // during Main::cleanup(), causing use-after-free crashes when the Variant
    // ref-counts are decremented.
    global_array.clear();
    _global_array = nullptr;
    globals.clear();
    named_globals.clear();
    global_array_empty_indexes.clear();

    finishing = false;
}
```

### Steps to reproduce

Crash is not consistent, but I believe it requires a GDExtension that registers a RefCounted-derived singleton as a global. Run Godot with --import or any flow that triggers a clean shutdown. The crash is intermittent depending on memory layout.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

I don't believe I can make an MRP because I wasn't even changing the component that is associated with the crash when I started seeing this problem.
